member.name: T:KeshavSingh.Realtime.Calls.CallService
member.summary:
Group audio/video calls on top of chat conversations and scheduled meetings.
The server is a signalling server only: it decides who may call or be invited, relays each participant's SDP/ICE to the specific peer it is addressed to, keeps the roster, and logs that the call happened. Media never touches it — participants connect to each other in a **mesh** and WebRTC encrypts every stream end to end (DTLS-SRTP), so no call content can be recorded or intercepted here. The mesh is also why exists.
Every operation is scoped to the room's participants; anyone else gets NotFound, the same answer as an unknown room id, so a call's existence can't be probed (anti-IDOR).

member.name: T:KeshavSingh.Realtime.Calls.CallSession
member.summary:
The audit row for one call, in chat_calls. It records who was on and for how long — never any media (calls are peer-to-peer, DTLS-SRTP encrypted end to end) and never the SDP/ICE payloads, which contain network addresses.
Rows written before calls became multi-party rooms stored a caller/callee pair instead of a participant list. Those fields are still mapped (see the Legacy* properties) so old calls keep showing up in the log instead of breaking the read — the collection is an audit trail, so losing history to a schema change would be the wrong trade.
